timing.label: Objection 1 (technical)
timing.question: A plugin is one more supply chain to secure. Why should I let it run in every session?

timing.label: Objection 2 (commercial)
timing.question: Why not just hand each brand team a playbook and skip the packaging?

approach.quote: I made a skill for the release checklist

tag_question_examples: They're better, right? Everyone uses them.

must_mention.point: One plugin ships both procedures as skills together with the freeze rule, the push guard hook, the reviewer subagent and the incident MCP
Repository installs follow the branch unless pinned to a SHA, uploads stay pinned to what was uploaded, and a skills-only repo needs no manifest
must_mention.evidence_quote: A repo install keeps up with the branch unless you pin a SHA. Uploads stay as uploaded and skills-only repos need no manifest

must_mention.point: A new uploaded revision replaces the whole bundle, so a partial zip removes every file it left out
The MCP credential is connected after install through a secret reference and never written into the plugin files
Engineers without edit rights can only propose; an admin approves the diff before the shared plugin changes

sentences_to_rerecord: And I put the PagerDuty key in the config for now so the demo works.
The hook guarantees nobody pushes to main, even in cloud sessions.
They're better, right? Everyone uses them.

accuracy.anchor: One of five points; the token was placed in the plugin and the revision described as a patch. (anchors: 27–30 every point with a file or scope named; 15–20 three of five; under 10 one point)

structure.anchor: No outcome, no evidence, no ask; feature talk throughout. (anchors: 22–25 all parts in order; 13–17 parts present but weak; under 8 problem only)

customer_relevance.anchor: Did not answer what runs, where it came from or who can change it. (anchors: 16–20 reviewer's questions answered with files, scopes and counts; 10–13 some; under 6 feature talk)

brevity_and_fluency.anchor: Five of six segments off target; eleven fillers and two long pauses. (anchors: 11–15 segments on target, under 1 filler/min; 6–8 two or more segments off; under 4 most segments off)

recovery.anchor: Neither objection acknowledged; objection 1 relied on trust in the team, objection 2 on popularity. (anchors: 7–10 acknowledge → boundary → evidence → offer held with numbers; 4–6 partial; under 3 no pattern)

stems: "Every session will get…" — lead with the outcome, then the contents.
"The token is not in the plugin; it is…" — rehearse the credential answer until it is one sentence.
"You are right that it is new code…" — acknowledge before you defend.
previous_run_comparison: First recorded run for dryrun on lab 04; no previous run to compare with.
